![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/68359143b50b4d6187f2d50793b1d3cb4b48656f1996cd222cb5d07f666b535e.png)

The region enclosed by the curve $y=-1-x,$ the vertical line $x=-3,$ and the horizontal line $y=0$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=-3,$ as shown in the picture. Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
Since our region rotates about a vertical line, we need to write the equation of the given curve in terms of $y:$ 

$$
y=-1-x\,⟹\,x=-1-y
$$

 

Now, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curve and the line $x=-3$ by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-1-y & =-3 \\ y & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=2$ along the $y$-axis.

To determine which is the left and which is the right function, let's draw our horizontal arrow.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/73d5da7e1bd4b409574f6e9ab034dde51012eb956b3ea72a3529f7d432fe781d.png)

 

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=-3,$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=-1-y.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[\,(\text{right function})-(\text{left function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}{[\,(-1-y)-(-3)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}{(2-y)}^{2}\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}({y}^{2}-4y+4)\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
